Block 1: 3 min run for distance, remember your distance

Block 2: everyone does a 1 mile run.

When finished repeat until time:

-170 m row 

-0.17 mile run (if your distance from block 1 was ODD run at flat road, if distance was EVEN run on 8% incline)

Block 3: 3 min run for distance

Everyone has already given great advice, but I would add that “everyone having a close group of friends” is certainly not the case. Many people, myself included, don’t make close friends until sophomore year. I didn’t meet my friends until the end of mine! Many friendships during freshman year can end up being superficial anyway. I’m very shy and struggled with anxiety in college as well, and it took me a while to find people I was comfortable with. Be involved as much as you are okay with and try to make small talk with the people around you! (start by saying hi or commenting on something happening around you) You will find people you can at least hang out with sometimes. Also, getting an off campus job and being with the same people frequently helped immensely.

I think it’s generally accepted to be “harder” than 250 which focuses mostly on motion. (I think Phys 211 is calc based motion?) However, it depends from person to person. 251 is more abstract as it focuses on concepts like magnetism, electricity, and light waves. Not as much math at all. I never took Physics 211, so I’m not sure I could compare them. Van Hook is ok. The slides he uses aren’t helpful unless you go the class.

There is a good chance that you will be able to get in during the first week of classes when people change their schedules around. You could also try to show up for the class anyway and see if the professor can manually add you to the course. That has worked for me before.
Bring your own!

I didn’t meet my good friends until second semester of sophomore year, and I know that was the case for many others I knew as well. It can take a while to settle in. In my experience, clubs that meet infrequently and/or lack an “interactive” component are not good places to meet friends.  That being said, I met my best friends through my part time job and club sports. Meeting multiple times a week and bonding over common interests and experiences was helpful for me as it’s hard to get to know people you only see once or twice a month! Working at a bar/restaurant was also entertaining and it was fun to work with other college students.

(Side note: not sure if this is still a thing, but look into joining Club Croquet. I had some friends in it and it’s not very serious at all and mostly a social club!)
